options.title: Marvel Put Captain America Up as Collateral
options.first_line: Marvel borrowed the money for its own movies, and the security was Captain America.
options.first_frame: A Captain America comic cover pushing in, the name Marvel slamming in between the layers.

options.title: Marvel Pledged {fact3} Heroes for One Loan
options.first_line: Marvel handed a bank the film rights to {fact3} of its heroes, just to make one movie.
options.first_frame: A wall of Marvel comic covers punching in one after another, a red stamp PLEDGED landing over them.

options.title: Bankrupt Marvel Bet Its Own Heroes on a Loan
options.first_line: A few years after going bankrupt, Marvel bet its own heroes on a bank loan.
options.first_frame: Marvel's 1996 bankruptcy filing page with the word bankrupt highlighted, then a cut to a Captain America comic.

why: Captain America, a hero everyone can picture, pledged as loan collateral raises an instant 'how, and what happened?' that only the video answers, and the comic cover with Marvel slamming in reads without sound.
